svg.text: Current implemented RTL · 4 resident warps · 4 lanes per warp · 32-bit instructions and data
Inputs: clock / reset, run enable, warp launch (ID, PC, mask), debug register preload
Status: issue / stalls, warp state, register operands / ALU result, bank conflicts, branch masks and reconvergence
Block or retry a candidate; issue only when ready
Accept also advances scheduler and warp control
Mark on issue; clear on commit
Normal reads use the selected warp; TMUL owns both read ports for four gather cycles
Debug preload has priority over architectural writes
FP in-flight · tensor ready / gather · writeback space
Check all A / B / C rows against pending destinations
EXIT waits until the warp has no pending writes
Rejoin handling takes priority over the fetched operation
register checks / destination allocation on issue
OPERANDS + ISSUED OPERATION · opcode, warp, active mask, PC and immediate
Wait for active lanes; retain result + context
One SIMD FP instruction in flight
Fixed 4×4 FP32 · one tensor job in flight
Gather A + B in 4 register-read cycles
Save warp / mask; reserve 4 destination rows
Pack the 16 output words into 4 vector writes
Load 32 input words; stream 16 result words
Feeder staggers the row / column inputs
Each PE: multiply → add → local C register
A moves right; B moves down; C stays
Advance only when every PE finishes
Non-fused MAC · release destinations on final row commit
Priority: completed FP → tensor row → integer result / shared-memory load
One 128-bit result + saved warp, destination register and active-lane mask
Commit when the register port is available; hold pending results during debug writes
FP / tensor hold results; integer / loads retry when writeback is busy
REGISTER COMMIT: write active lanes · clear busy state · release the final tensor row
Clock / reset apply across the SM.
Functional block diagram of snackwell_sm / multiwarp_execution_core. Connections show data and control flow; they do not imply one pipeline stage per box.
